name: figma-comment

frames.best_why: Comment card is fully open with readable author, time and complete message over the canvas.

tagline: Design comment pins that spring open into author, time and message.
summary: Small avatar pins sit on a mock design canvas. Clicking one expands it into a rounded card showing who wrote it, when, and their comment, and an outside click closes it.
appearance: Round avatar pins scattered over a dark mock landing page. An open one becomes a dark rounded card with the avatar at its top left, a bold name, a muted time, and a few lines of light message text.
behaviour: Clicking a pin spring-expands it into the comment card while the avatar slides in from the corner. The text fades and unblurs into place, and clicking outside collapses it back to a round pin.
demo_content: Mock landing hero labelled 'Landing / Hero: Desktop' with comments from Maya Chen, Leo Park and Ana Ruiz.
use_when: Reviewers need to leave or read notes anchored to a spot on a design, mockup or prototype.
avoid_when: You need a threaded conversation with replies; the card shows only one author and message.
customise: Author, avatar, message, timestamp, width and position class are all props. Card colours, radius and the spring are set in the source.
weight_why: One avatar, a short card and a single spring plus blur transition; nothing loops.

a11y.note: The pin is a div with a click handler, so it cannot be opened from the keyboard or announced as a control.

props.name: message
props.default: What happens if we adjust this to handle a light and dark mode? I'm not sure if we're ready to handle...

issues: The pin trigger is a non-focusable div, so keyboard users cannot open a comment.
Frame 5 catches the card mid-blur, so its text is not readable.
polish_why: Crisp spring expansion and blurred text reveal; pins read clearly against the dark canvas.
